section.title: Overview
section.para: A gazetteer maps place names to place records. The opennlp.tools.geo.Gazetteer interface is what every lookup goes through: a bundled table, a downloaded dataset, an ingested database, and a remote service client are all implementations of this one interface, and any of them can be handed to the components that consume it. Each record is a GazetteerEntry carrying the canonical and alternate names, a point location, an optional bounding box, the ISO 3166-1 country code, a coarse feature class, the population, and dataset-specific extras as provenance-tagged attributes.

The opennlp-geo module ships four file-backed implementations: BundledGazetteer over the bundled Natural Earth populated-places table, GeoNamesGazetteer over a user-downloaded GeoNames extract, OvertureGazetteer over an Overture divisions export, and UserGazetteer over a user-authored file, each described in its own section below. An InMemoryGazetteer builds the same index over caller-supplied entries, so place records from a database or a service compose without a file in between. All are immutable and thread-safe after loading, so one instance can be shared across threads.

section.title: User-supplied places
section.para: UserGazetteer loads places a public dataset does not know, for example customer sites or internal facility names, from a user-authored file, so they take part in geocoding and everything downstream of it. The file holds one place per line with tab-separated columns in this order, where trailing columns may be omitted and an empty column means absent: record id, canonical name, alternate names separated by |, latitude, longitude, country code, feature class, population, bounding box as west,south,east,north, containment chain separated by |, and one key=value attribute per further column. Lines starting with # and blank lines are skipped.

A row needs either both coordinates or a bounding box; with only a bounding box the point location becomes the box's center. Free-text metadata such as a postal address belongs in an attribute column: it is carried verbatim on the entry and is never parsed or matched. The following file, whose columns are separated by single tab characters, defines a plant with an address attribute and a campus located through its bounding box alone.
# id name alternates lat lon cc class pop bbox containment attributes plant-3 Acme Plant 3 Plant 3|The Plant 33.75 -84.39 US POI 0 Georgia|Fulton County address=123 Main St, Atlanta GA 30303 campus-east Acme Campus East US POI 0 -84.5,33.6,-84.2,33.9

section.title: GeoNames tables
section.para: GeoNamesGazetteer loads a table in the GeoNames main format, such as the filtered city extracts published on the GeoNames export site. The user downloads the extract; nothing is bundled, and the publisher's license terms, including attribution, stay with the downloaded file. The whole table is indexed in memory, so the loader is meant for the filtered extracts rather than the full dump.

section.title: Overture division tables
Overlaying a base gazetteer
section.para: OverlayGazetteer composes a base gazetteer with user-supplied changes: additions from a second gazetteer, and suppression rules hiding base entries. Consumers see one merged view through the same Gazetteer interface, so every component downstream picks the changes up without knowing they exist. Additions rank first in lookups. Suppressions hide entries of the base only, never additions, so a rule plus an addition with the same name replaces a base entry.

A suppression rule is a place name with optional country and feature-class filters, one rule per line with tab-separated columns. The following file removes the city of Mobile, Alabama, from a corpus where that reading is always noise, while leaving every other Mobile-named record intact.
# name country feature class Mobile US CITY

section.title: Bringing your own implementation
section.para: The interface is registry-free: implementing its four methods is all it takes, there is nothing to declare or register anywhere, and the instance is handed to whatever consumes the interface, typically as the additions side of an OverlayGazetteer. An implementation must document its own name-matching semantics and its thread-safety guarantees; the implementations shipped here are immutable and safe to share between threads. Because the contract is one plain constructor-built object, an implementation also drops directly into any dependency-injection container as a bean, with no framework types anywhere in OpenNLP.
